comment: TLB is knowledgeable and caring, and his class was one of my favorites this semester. Lectures are not always the most engaging as they go over the same content you were supposed to have just read. On the other hand, if you pay attention in class and get your assignments done, you should be very prepared for his tests. Labs were super fun!

Professor Lookingbill is one of my favorite professors. He makes an effort to get to know each of his students. He makes the classroom a comfortable learning environment. Exams were somewhat difficult and reading is required. Meeting with him during office hours is very beneficial.

I loved Professor Lookingbill as a professor, he always made our class periods and labs fun and exciting. It also helped that we had a great class. His class is mostly lectures, but we get into deeper discussions. As a non-geography-focused student, I thought this would be challenging for me, but he is always available to help.

Feedback was rarely given unless specifically asked. Weekly online quizzes straight from the textbook, but reading the textbook isn't really necessary. Tests were straight from the lecture (except the few oddly specific questions from the textbook). Lecture was him reading from the slides. Lab was usually making maps or collecting data.

Important to be there- things on the exam are directly related to what we discuss in class- like to the word. Important to pay attention but very straight-forward. He's fair and approachable. Lectures were us sitting and him sitting talking about the slide- a little tedious. Readings felt less necessary since exams were about in-class conversations

Todd is such a dad, super nice and cares about students. Subject itself boring, and labs are long and aren't really related to what we learn in class. Write ups are difficult and confusing. Group collab often in class and out, and encourages discussion amongst heavy lectures. Would take for an easier science, but chem in cooking or art is easier

TLB is a fantastic professor who clearly cares about students and wants us to understand the material. While this class (Biogeography) doesn't have a lab, there was a good mix of lectures and activities over the semester. There is a good bit of reading/homework but I expected that of a 300 level course and they were outlined in the syllabus.

Todd can be a tough grader and have ambiguous grading standards at times, which I think is worth pointing out. However, I have worked closely with him, and he is by far one of the most passionate and genuinely caring professors I have ever had. He is a really awesome guy, and I would encourage anyone to take a class with him and get to know him.

By far the worst class I've taken. Unreasonable amount of work and the exams aren't easy. Three exams, two presentations, three short presentations, weekly lab reports, final scientific research paper and project, weekly readings and quizzes, homework sheets. Not worth your time.

Have had Todd for more than one of his classes so I know him well. Really nice guy but bad professor. Todd isn't clear what he wants, doesn't grade anything until the last week of school. Loves stupid group projects and talking about random things that are factually incorrect. Worst professor I have had at Richmond, although I did get an A.

Love Todd, but not his class. He never provided feedback on any of our writing for the entire semester, the class was easy and I got an A, but never knew how I was doing for the entire semester. He also does not really make clear what he wants, ideas in his head apply to the entire class but he only tells one person and expects the rest to know.
TLB is the best.  Interesting and relevant lectures and all around just a great/funny guy. My favorite professor at UR

TLB has been my prof for multiple courses, my research mentor for two summers, etc. He is my favorite professor at UR. He won't let you get away with coasting, but he makes both the material and his expectations clear. Plus, he's a genuinely great person to be around.
Great Professor, extremely helpful and truly cares about the subject and his students.  Also a total genius

Todd Lookingbill (TLB) is my FAVORITE teacher at UR. Aside from being a total genius, he is unbelievably cool and cares a lot about his subject-matter and students. IMO the best teacher at UR and the predominating proportion of Geography/Environmental/Biology students here agree.
